question: What did the actual customers say in the calls supporting that conclusion?

answer.answer_markdown:
**The customers are not complaining that they lost the dispute; they are complaining that nobody looked.** Read in their own words, the same sentence comes back again and again: the claim was denied for lack of evidence that the bank never asked for, or the evidence they did send was never acknowledged.

Three shapes recur. Denied without a request for evidence. A temporary credit handed back and then reversed, with nothing produced to explain the reversal. And a claim closed on a technicality: a reporting deadline, a dispute window, or the word "authorized", rather than on what actually happened to the customer.

This is the same story across every product and most of the country, in hundreds of different wordings, so it is a process behaviour rather than a handful of bad cases. The customers are asking for something cheap: tell me what you looked at, and ask me for what you are missing before you close the case.

Two changes follow directly from what they say. Before any denial for insufficient evidence, the case must show a documented request to the customer. And every denial letter should name the records the decision relied on, so the customer can answer them instead of starting over.

claims.statement: Across the contacts in this theme, customers describe fraud and transaction disputes being denied, or provisional credits reversed, without the bank reviewing, requesting or producing the evidence.

confidence.badge: broad pattern · 394 calls · 24 months · 6 products · 41 states

quotes.quote: they will only review the matter if I provide the full, official statement
quotes.why: The bank refuses to look until the customer supplies a document it will not justify asking for.

quotes.quote: call Chase bank back to give them polic report number and to ask them to stop payment because transaction is still pending but they said they can not do that.
quotes.why: Reported while the payment was still pending, and still denied as authorized.

quotes.quote: yet somehow can not locate a single piece of paper : my alleged signed authorization.
quotes.why: The bank cannot produce the authorization it says exists.

quotes.quote: They said they couldnt do anything as it wasnt reported in 5 days. How could I report it when they insisted it went to the right place.
quotes.why: A deadline the customer could not have met, because the bank kept saying nothing was wrong.

quotes.quote: Waiting the entire 18 months, we again contacted Chase, advising them XXXX had done absolutely NOTHING to cancel our timeshare. But Chase then told us : A ) The clock had run out on this dispute, and B ) Once a dispute has been closed, it can not be re-opened.
quotes.why: The customer waits the window the bank set, then is told the window has closed.

quotes.quote: Chase initially provided a temporary credit, which was later reversed after they determined the transactions were authorized. However, Chase has failed to provide any evidence supporting this conclusion.
quotes.why: Provisional credit reversed, with no evidence shown for the reversal.

quotes.quote: Despite that, Chase denied reimbursement of the remaining $3700.00. Chase stated only that it did not find evidence to support reimbursement and directed me to continue working directly with the merchant because the merchant initiated the transactions.
quotes.why: Denied, sent back to the merchant, and never shown the records behind the decision.

quotes.quote: Chase denied the dispute, claiming the transaction was not eligible.
quotes.why: Denied for lack of evidence the bank never asked for.

caveats: This is a complaint corpus: it records the customers who escalated, not the disputes that were resolved quietly.
Complaint dates lag the contact they describe, so the month shown is when the customer wrote, not when the denial happened.
The quotes are the customers' account of the decision; the bank's case file was not available to check against.
Quotes are redacted at source, so names, dates and case numbers appear as XXXX.
